messages:
Omar: Idea: introduce 'deploy profiles' as a compact way to encode pin, traffic policy, change window, and fallback. one command to run a profile.
Omar: Sketch command:
```
/ship profile payments-pulse --pin v4.0.0 --window 2026-05-10T12:00Z/2026-05-10T13:00Z --pulse 10% --notify #payments-oncall --preview
```
Nina: Nice. Pulse instead of canary sounds less overloaded. Can profiles express multi-stage promos?
Omar: Yep. profile YAML lists stages (staging -> pulse -> ramp) with gate checks. promotion can be automatic or manual.
Ben: Rollback ergonomics: `/ship rollback --profile payments-pulse --to last_good --note "latency spike"` should create a revert and tag the original deploy.
Talia: Ops asks: profiles should support `sensitivity: high|low` to require approval, and `fallback: pinned_stable` when last_good is unsafe.
ship-bot: Created draft release note rn-20260510-001 for profile payments-pulse. Use `/ship rn edit rn-20260510-001`.
Nina: Also add `/ship explain` so reviewers see step-by-step plan + metric checks. reviewers love diffs.
Ben: Small automation snippet for watch-and-roll:
```
# monitor and auto rollback after sustained breach
if ops-metrics query --deploy $ID --window 5m --error_rate > 0.6; then
  /ship rollback --id $ID --to last_good --message "auto-rollback: sustained errors"
fi
```
Talia: I'll draft a PR template and a short escape-hatch cheatsheet for release playbooks.
Omar: I'll open the repo PR with profile schema + ship-bot handlers tomorrow. tagging payments and ops for review.
